newsitem.title: LEBANON: Most Beirut shares unchanged in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Most Beirut shares unchanged in quiet trade.

text.p: Two shares fell as the Beirut Stock Exchange opened the week quietly on Monday with most of the active shares unchanged.
The LIBX bank index fell 0.53 percent to 152.96. The LISPI general index fell 0.25 percent to 89.20, while the BLOM general index fell 0.35 percent to 928.83.
Turnover rose to 121,565 shares from 93,651 and value was $1,570,764 from $1,277,153.

"A lot of investors are accumulating bank shares on the perception that banks' mid-year earnings are going to be very good," Nicholas Sawan, Deputy Manager and head of trading at Beirut Finance House Lebanon Invest said.
Of the three listed banks, Bank of Beirut fell to $3.875 from $3.937. Banque Audi maintained its alltime high of $23.25 and Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce was unchanged at $18.
Trading was quiet because "investors are buying shares in an intelligent way so as not to bring prices higher", Sawan told Reuters.
Solidere was mixed in strong demand. Solidere B hares fell to $10.625 from $10.75 while A shares traded unchanged at $10.5. The shares traded in strong demand.
Ciments Libanais was unchanged at $1.28125 on turnover of 5,000 shares. There was no trade in the three other industrial companies: Ciment Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
